facts.value: Are you interested in Science? Are you concerned about the quality of our environment? Would you like a career helping to make improvements to our environment for the benefit of this and future generations? Do you want to understand more about the global and national challenges of climate change and sustainability? Then perhaps you should study Environmental Science at UL.
This course will help you understand more about global challenges around climate change and sustainability in preparation for a career to tackle these issues.
Entry route to this degree at UL is via LM123 Biological and Chemical Sciences Common Entry.
There is also a direct entry route to this course via LM066 Environmental Science.

The Environmental Science program at the University of Limerick is distinctive due to its relevance to industry and business, focusing on environmental technology, environmental management, sustainability, and health & safety in the workplace.
Environmental Science - the application of the fundamental sciences to environmental issues.

Environmental Management – the assessment of a broad range of issues around global warming and sustainability, and how strategies can be developed and implemented to protect and sustain all aspects of the environment.
Clean Technology - the use of cleaner technologies and processes to minimize the negative impacts of technology on the environment.
Waste Management - the study of the physical methodologies and techniques for dealing with increasing levels of waste generated by the manufacturer and consumer.
Health & Safety - a complementary area to environmental science which specifically deals with significant health and safety issues both in the workplace and in outdoor environments.
The co-op experience was probably the highlight of the course experience. I worked at Irish Cement Ltd, in Drogheda Co. Louth, for my placement.
Worked with the plant’s Environmental Manager as part of the Environmental team.
Gained hands-on experience with sample collections and experience in filling out the first Annual Environmental Report.
Had the opportunity to work with the EPA and Natura and was invited to the annual environmental review meeting held between the Limerick and Drogheda Irish Cement sites.
My favorite part of the Co-op was the opportunity to meet and work with consultants in the field.
The goal is to own my own environmental consultancy.
The course features chemistry, biology, and geography, along with field work and lab work.
